en: The season of the northeast monsoon
Standing alone in the slanting wind and fine rain
Low deer-grass spreads loosely along the path
As if a page turned open
Chapter by chapter, verse by verse
Swaying with the white plumes of silvergrass
A white tragedy beyond all help
The battering waves of the years
Following the rise and fall of the tide
Rolling up surging waves of foam
Silent sorrow among the wild grass of the mountain hollow
Reaching out toward the sea's surface
Facing the clouded sky alone, wordless
How could it be only this lonely island
Rising from the depths of the sea
Green Island is truly a beautiful little island
Peaks stretch on, winding north and south
Facing the Pacific to the east
Water and sky, vast and boundless

zh: 希望囚禁於此的異鄉人
被無情歷史沾辱的淒楚
也是白色恐怖的受難者
en: The low, steady rhythm of waves breaking on the shore
The sea breeze brushing the sand, gentle and soft
Listening to her tender, plaintive whisper
Whether brought over by the Japanese
Or perhaps caught by the Chinese
She soothed each and every one of them
Understanding her goodwill and her helplessness
The bitter grief stained by an unfeeling history
Is also a part of Taiwan
Was also a victim of the White Terror

zh: 東北季風帶來連日陰霾
en: The northeast monsoon brings days of haze
Autumn's bitter wind and driving rain
One gust tighter than the last
Tear-tracks from a night of long weeping
The footprints of the crowds passing to and fro
Fishing boats in the harbor beyond the hill
Cry after cry, quietly fading into the distance

points.zh: 綠島舊名火燒島。日治時期開始，1911年，日本當局就在火燒島建立了第一座監獄，起初收容的是台灣各地的流氓。之後，才轉收犯人。在白色恐怖時期，二個政治犯監獄拘禁了許多政治犯。第一個是保安司令部新生訓導處 ( 1951‐1965 ) ，第 二個是國防部綠島感訓監獄 ( 1972‐1987，綠洲山莊 )。參觀綠洲山莊舊址時，頓覺人事蒼桑，時代流變難料，走在歷史的時間長廊和政治犯的監禁空間，時空交集，讓人深刻體㑹人權思想和具體運作的重要性，也期望人權體制落實成爲日常生活的一部分。
points.en: Green Island was formerly known as Huoshao Island (Fire-Burned Island). Beginning in the Japanese colonial period, in 1911 the Japanese authorities established the island's first prison, which initially held hooligans and vagrants rounded up from around Taiwan, before later being converted to hold prisoners generally. During the White Terror period, two political prisons held large numbers of political prisoners: the first was the Garrison Command's New Life Correction Center (1951–1965), and the second was the Ministry of National Defense's Green Island Reform Prison (1972–1987, Oasis Villa). Visiting the former site of Oasis Villa, one is struck by the vicissitudes of human affairs and the unpredictability of historical change. Walking through this corridor of historical time and the confined spaces where political prisoners were held, past and present intersect, deepening one's appreciation of the importance of human rights ideals and their concrete implementation, and one hopes that a human rights system will truly become part of everyday life.

points.zh: 綠洲山莊監獄的視聽展覧室內，放映的記錄影片中，受難者追憶，如何被驅迫到海邊，赤手搬運沉重的嘍咕礁岩，在山坳荒草，堆砌築造牢房，囚禁自己。
points.en: In the audiovisual exhibition room of the Oasis Villa prison, a documentary film plays in which survivors recall how they were forced to the shore to carry heavy coral reef rocks by hand, and, amid the wild grass of the mountain hollows, to build with their own hands the very cells that would imprison them.

points.zh:
綠島人權紀念碑上，銘刻柏楊的一段話 :
「在那個時代，有多少母親，爲她們囚禁在這個島上的孩子，長夜哭泣。」
簡短數語，道盡那個時代，不爲人知的辛酸和哀愁。
points.en:
Inscribed on the Green Island Human Rights Memorial is a passage by Bo Yang:
"In that era, how many mothers wept through long nights for the children imprisoned on this island."
In just a few short words, it conveys all the unspoken bitterness and sorrow of that era.

points.zh: 綠島人權文化園區位於將軍岩前方，涵蓋人權紀念公園，綠洲山莊，莊敬營區，綠島技能訓練所，和燕子洞等。綠洲山莊爲白色恐怖時期，囚禁政治犯和思想犯之處。綠洲山莊保留了昔日高聳的圍牆，鐡絲網，操場，禮堂和八卦樓 (監獄區，該建築自上空俯看狀似八卦)。山莊内展示許多白色恐怖時期相關資料。八卦樓的監獄囚房，窄小沉悶，籠罩着幽暗沉重的氛圍，卽使在多年後的現在，那份沉重仍然揮之不去。綠島人權紀念公園是台灣知名建築師漢寶德所設計，於2002年12月10日世界人權日正式開放。白色的建築外觀，具有和平的意象，也象徵着跟「白色恐佈時期」正式告別，邁向民主公義的新時代。紀念碑潛入地下的設計 (按: 華裔林璎所設計的美國華盛頓越戰紀念碑，也是潛入地下的建築) ，象徵被掩蓋在檔案文献暗處的慘淡塺史，被漠視歧視的不公不義，以及不得伸張的苦楚屈辱。長條狀的人權紀念碑，又稱爲「垂淚碑」，䥴刻着昔日政治犯的姓名和受刑時日。螺旋狀的斜向走道，在下雨時，雨水會由兩旁的渠道匯入垂淚池，象徵着受刑犯親人以及所有台灣人爲之滴落的眼淚。人權紀念公園濱海處有將軍岩和三峰岩，是突出於海岬的黑色譙岩，狀似身披戰甲的將軍和三位站立的小兵。又可眺望牛頭山，是一個兼具歷史意義和自然景觀的的特色景點。
points.en: The Green Island Human Rights Culture Park is located in front of General Rock, encompassing the Human Rights Memorial Park, Oasis Villa, Zhuangjing Camp, the Green Island Vocational Training Center, and Swallow Cave, among others. Oasis Villa was the site where political prisoners and prisoners of conscience were held during the White Terror period. It preserves the once-towering perimeter walls, barbed wire, exercise yard, auditorium, and the Bagua Building (the prison block, so named because, viewed from above, the building resembles the eight trigrams). Inside the villa many materials related to the White Terror period are on display. The prison cells of the Bagua Building are narrow and oppressive, shrouded in a dim, heavy atmosphere that, even now, many years later, has never quite lifted. The Green Island Human Rights Memorial Park was designed by the renowned Taiwanese architect Han Pao-teh and was formally opened on December 10, 2002, World Human Rights Day. The white exterior of the building carries an image of peace, symbolizing a formal farewell to the "White Terror era" and a step into a new age of democracy and justice. The design of the monument sinking into the ground (note: the Vietnam Veterans Memorial in Washington, D.C., designed by the Chinese-American architect Maya Lin, is likewise a structure that sinks into the earth) symbolizes the bleak history buried in the shadows of archival documents, the injustice of being ignored and discriminated against, and the suffering and humiliation that could never be redressed. The elongated Human Rights Memorial, also known as the "Monument of Tears," is inscribed with the names of former political prisoners and the dates of their imprisonment. Along the spiraling sloped walkway, when it rains, rainwater flows through channels on either side into the Pool of Tears, symbolizing the tears shed by the prisoners' families and by all the people of Taiwan on their behalf. Along the coast of the Human Rights Memorial Park stand General Rock and Three Peaks Rock, black reef formations jutting out from the headland that resemble a general clad in armor together with three standing soldiers. From here one can also gaze out at Oxhead Mountain, making this a landmark that combines both historical significance and natural scenery.
